{{Short description|American basketball player (born 2003)}} {{Use American English|date=March 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=March 2026}} {{Infobox basketball biography | name = Jaylen Wells | image = Jaylen Wells (240910-F-UM667-4692) (cropped).jpg | image_size = | caption = Wells with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in 2024 | position = [[Small forward]] | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 7 | weight_lb = 205 | league = [[NBA]] | team = Memphis Grizzlies | number = 0 | birth_date = {{birth date and age|2003|8|26}} | birth_place = [[Sacramento, California]], U.S. | high_school = [[Folsom High School|Folsom]]
([[Folsom, California]]) | college = * [[Sonoma State Seawolves men's basketball|Sonoma State]] (2021–2023) * [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State]] (2023–2024) | draft_year = 2024 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 39 | draft_team = [[Memphis Grizzlies]] | career_start = 2024 | years1 = {{nbay|2024|start}}–present | team1 = [[Memphis Grizzlies]] | highlights = * [[NBA All-Rookie Team|NBA All-Rookie First Team]] ({{nbay|2024|end}}) * [[California Collegiate Athletic Association|CCAA]] Player of the Year (2023) * First-team All-CCAA (2023) }} '''Jaylen Wells''' (born August 26, 2003) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Sonoma State Seawolves men's basketball|Sonoma State Seawolves]] and the [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State Cougars]]. ==Early life and high school career== Wells grew up in [[Sacramento, California]] and attended [[Folsom High School]].{{cite web |last=Davidson |first=Joe |date=July 10, 2022 |title=Trio of young Sacramento players train against pros |url=https://www.sacbee.com/sports/high-school/article262985473.html |access-date=May 14, 2024 |work=[[The Sacramento Bee]]}} As a senior, he averaged 26.3 points, 3.2 rebounds and 1.2 assists per game. He was named the area Player of the Year by ''[[The Sacramento Bee]]''.{{cite web |last=Mascareñas |first=Xavier |date=July 7, 2021 |title=Bee's Best Basketball Players of the Year, Harriel and Wells |url=https://www.sacbee.com/sports/high-school/article252297233.html |access-date=May 14, 2024 |work=[[The Sacramento Bee]]}} Wells committed to play [[college basketball]] at [[NCAA Division II|Division II]] [[Sonoma State University]].{{cite web |last=Long |first=Matt |date=May 27, 2021 |title=Jaylen Wells can do it all on the court |url=https://goldcountrymedia.com/news/189808/jaylen-wells-can-do-it-all-on-the-court/ |access-date=May 14, 2024 |work=Gold Country Media}} ==College career== Wells began his college basketball career playing for the [[Sonoma State Seawolves]].{{cite web |last=Morris |first=Gus |date=March 21, 2024 |title=Former SSU star helps Washington State to NCAA Tournament |url=https://www.pressdemocrat.com/article/sports/college-notebook-former-ssu-star-jaylen-wells-helps-washington-state-to-nc/ |access-date=May 13, 2024 |work=[[The Press Democrat]]}} He averaged 12.6 points per game during his freshman season.{{cite web |last=Clark |first=Colton |date=April 18, 2023 |title=Jaylen Wells, a Division II All-American from Sonoma State, transfers to Washington State |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2023/apr/18/jaylen-wells-a-division-ii-all-american-from-sonom/ |access-date=May 13, 2024 |work=[[The Spokesman-Review]]}} He was named the [[California Collegiate Athletic Association]] Player of the Year after averaging 22.4 points per game during his sophomore campaign.{{cite web |last=Morris |first=Gus |date=March 16, 2023 |title=College notebook: SSU's Jaylen Wells named conference Player of the Year |url=https://www.pressdemocrat.com/article/sports/college-notebook-ssus-jaylen-wells-named-to-division-ii-all-region-basket/ |access-date=May 13, 2024 |work=[[The Press Democrat]]}} After the season, he entered the [[NCAA transfer portal]].{{cite web |last=Vinnick |first=Jamey |date=July 4, 2023 |title=WSU basketball: The file on 6-7 forward Jaylen Wells |url=https://247sports.com/college/washington-state/article/wsu-basketball-jaylen-wells-file-on-6-7-forward-212246970/ |access-date=May 14, 2024 |website=[[247Sports]]}} Wells transferred to [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State]] and entered his junior season as the Cougars' starting [[small forward]].{{cite web |last=Woods |first=Greg |date=December 16, 2023 |title=Behind the transformation of WSU guard Jaylen Wells, and his elite shooting |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/wsu-cougar-basketball/behind-the-transformation-of-wsu-mens-basketball-guard-jaylen-wells-and-his-elite-shooting/ |access-date=May 13, 2024 |work=[[The Seattle Times]]}} He averaged 12.6 points and 4.6 rebounds per game.{{cite web |last=Vinnick |first=Jamey |date=April 30, 2024 |title=WSU's Jaylen Wells says entire focus is on NBA, not transfer portal |url=https://247sports.com/college/washington-state/article/jaylen-wells-wsu-basketball-says-entire-focus-is-on-nba-not-transfer-portal-231235506/ |access-date=May 13, 2024 |website=[[247Sports]]}} After the season, Wells declared for the [[2024 NBA draft]] while retaining his college eligibility.{{cite web |last=Woods |first=Greg |date=April 4, 2024 |title=WSU wing Jaylen Wells declares for NBA Draft, retaining option to return to school |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2024/apr/04/wsu-wing-jaylen-wells-declares-for-nba-draft-retai/ |access-date=May 13, 2024 |work=[[The Spokesman-Review]]}} He later also re-entered the transfer portal.{{cite web |last=Woods |first=Greg |date=April 25, 2024 |title=WSU men's wing Jaylen Wells reportedly entering transfer portal |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/wsu-cougar-basketball/wsu-mens-wing-jaylen-wells-reportedly-entering-transfer-portal/ |access-date=May 13, 2024 |work=[[The Seattle Times]]}} Wells later decided to remain in the draft.{{cite web |last=Woods |first=Greg |date=May 30, 2024 |title=Former WSU wing Jaylen Wells staying in NBA draft pool |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/wsu-cougar-basketball/former-wsu-wing-jaylen-wells-staying-in-nba-draft-pool/ |access-date=May 31, 2024 |work=[[The Seattle Times]]}} ==Professional career== On June 27, 2024, Wells was selected with the 39th overall pick by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in the [[2024 NBA draft]];{{cite web |last=Flojo |first=Enzo |date=June 28, 2024 |title=Grizzlies 2024 NBA Draft grades for every pick |url=https://clutchpoints.com/grizzlies-2024-nba-draft-grades-every-pick |access-date=June 28, 2024 |website=ClutchPoints}} on July 6, he signed with the Grizzlies.{{cite tweet |number=1809706546542076126 |user=GrizzliesPR |title=The Memphis Grizzlies today signed Zach Edey and Jaylen Wells to multi-year contracts. |author=Grizzlies PR |date=July 6, 2024 |access-date=July 14, 2024}} On October 23, Wells made his NBA debut, playing in a 126–124 victory over the [[2024–25 Utah Jazz season|Utah Jazz]] in the season opener. On October 31, Wells made his first career start against the [[2024–25 Milwaukee Bucks season|Milwaukee Bucks]] where he scored a then career-high 16 points. On December 3, Wells was named Western Conference Rookie of the Month for games played in October/November. It marks the 16th time a [[Memphis Grizzlies]] player has won the honor.{{cite web |title=Memphis Grizzlies Awards By Type|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/nba/teams/Memphis-Grizzlies/14/Awards/Type |access-date=December 13, 2024 |website=realGM.com}} In 20 games, Wells averaged 12.2 points, 3.3 rebounds and 1.9 assists in 25 minutes while shooting over 45 percent from the court.{{cite web |date=December 3, 2024 |title=Jaylen Wells named Western Conference Rookie of the month |url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/jaylen-wells-named-western-conference-rookie-of-the-month |access-date=December 5, 2024 |website=NBA.com}} On April 8, 2025, Wells suffered a broken right wrist in a game against the [[2024–25 Charlotte Hornets season|Charlotte Hornets]], ending his rookie season.{{cite web | last=Battifarano | first=Andrew | title=Grizzlies' Jaylen Wells stretchered off after suffering scary injury on flagrant foul | website=New York Post | date=2025-04-09 | url=https://nypost.com/2025/04/08/sports/grizzlies-jaylen-wells-stretchered-off-after-scary-injury-on-flagrant-foul/ | access-date=2025-12-06}} The injury came just days before the postseason that the Grizzlies had recently clinched.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/44044200/nba-postseason-tracker-clinched-playoff-play-spots|website=espn.com|title=NBA postseason tracker: Who clinched playoff, play-in spots?|date=April 8, 2025}} His 10.4 points per game ranked fourth among eligible rookies that season.{{Cite web|title=Stephon Castle has put up the most points per game by a rookie this season, with 14.5 per game.|url=https://www.statmuse.com/nba/ask?q=nba+rookie+points+per+game+leaders+2024-25|date=April 8, 2025|website=statmuse.com}} Wells started 69 games for Memphis during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], recording averages of 12.5 points, 3.2 rebounds, and 1.6 assists. On March 29, 2026, it was announced that Wells would require season-ending surgery to address a tendon [[avulsion fracture]] in his right big toe.{{Cite web|title=Jaylen Wells to undergo season-ending toe surgery|url=https://www.localmemphis.com/article/sports/basketball/grizzlies-jaylen-wells-surgery/522-67cd9a25-5c56-4f59-b31a-0cbfb3d5db15|access-date=June 11, 2026|website=localmemphis.com|language=en}} ==Personal life== In April 2025, it was reported that Wells had founded Sleep Nation with his high school friend, Ad Alsamariae, to help youths to achieve success in their sports careers.{{cite web |last=Bryant |first=Kailee |date=April 18, 2025 |title=Childhood friends lift Sacramento's unseen athletes through 'Sleep Nation' movement |url=https://www.abc10.com/article/news/local/nba-jaylen-wells-ad-alsamariae-sleep-nation-sacramento-movement/103-29079dc5-70f2-4740-8072-27bf6d7b139c |access-date=December 18, 2025 |work=[[KXTV|ABC
